mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Official Corporate Registry Extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent District Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea (Court Administration Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: official extract from the registry office then apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. Consular Legalization route for non-Apostille states: registry extract then Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication then legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate in the destination state. The routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; they must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and Corporate Seal Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean District Court Registry Office / authorized corporate seal certificate office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: certified seal certificate and current-status certificate then Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille. Consular Legalization route for non-Apostille states: certified documents then Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication then Korean consular legalization. Never use apostille and consular legalization together for the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa board of directors, notarized by a licensed Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by the Korean notary public then Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille for Hague Convention member states. For non-member states, notarization then Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication then legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are separate and mutually exclusive paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa incorporators, notarized by a licensed Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized Articles of Association then Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille if the receiving state is a Hague Apostille Convention member. If the receiving state is not a member, complete notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, and Korean consular legalization. Do not combine apostille with consular legalization in any sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank or foreign bank branch licensed in the Republic of Korea maintaining the corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer signature, notarization by the Korean notary, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille for Hague states; for non-Hague states, bank officer signature, notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then Korean consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service District Tax Office of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy of the business registration certificate, notarization if required by the receiving authority, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille for member states. For non-member states, use certified copy plus notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, and Korean consular legalization. The two authentication pathways are parallel and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders owning at least 25 percent, every director and officer, all beneficial owners, account signatories, and immediate family members must be screened before incorporation against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit sanctions list, the Korean Ministry of Strategy and Finance WMD financing list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated sanctions list, Interpol notices, and adverse media sources. A positive PEP or sanctions match triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth explanation, senior management approval, and immediate suspicious transaction reporting to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. Continuous daily monitoring must continue after incorporation and account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: I-Plus Internet Registration Office of the Korea Court Administration Office for corporate name availability and registration; National Tax Service HomeTax system for corporate business registration and tax identification
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory primary trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be written in Hangul, and a foreign-language or Romanized name may only be recorded after the Hangul name has been reserved. Foreign words in the name must be transliterated into Hangul pursuant to standard Korean language and orthography norms. The four-tier naming convention is applied: (1) distinctive enterprise token, (2) industry and business-purpose descriptor describing UN38.3 battery drop testing and CE-RED electromagnetic testing, (3) object clause as registered in the Articles of Association, and (4) mandatory suffix Yuhan Hoesa at the end. A full registry, trademark and KIPRIS conflict search is required before submission.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant obtains and preserves the written refusal note identifying the legal ground such as trademark conflict, prohibited word, or defective Hangul transliteration. Within the statutory objection window, file a written objection with the competent district court registry office, attaching a corrected proposed name, a fresh KIPRIS trademark search report, and evidence of prior use. If the registry maintains the refusal, file an immediate appeal through court administrative practice or, for trademark grounds, initiate a trial appeal before the Korean Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board. Engage Korean counsel before the deadline to avoid loss of the reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for this industry. The National Tax Service requires a physical business address for corporate business registration under the Value-Added Tax Act, while banks require a real lease contract, utility bill, corporate seal, and on-site inspection before a corporate account is opened. A virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address will be rejected because UN38.3 drop testing and CE-RED laboratory operations require physical premises, calibrated safety-testing equipment, dangerous-goods storage permits, and operational substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High likelihood, estimated at 70 to 85 percent within the first 12 months, because dangerous-goods battery testing triggers municipal tax, fire safety, and labor inspection. Checklist: (1) visible Yuhan Hoesa signboard at the registered office; (2) operational drop-test rig and shielded electromagnetic laboratory matching the registered business purpose; (3) lease agreements, utility bills, and corporate records at the site; (4) tax filings and employment records; (5) fire extinguishers, battery storage permits, and material safety data sheets; and (6) waste disposal contracts. Failure to maintain physical substance can lead to business registration cancellation and tax penalty liability.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Kyungje Hallimdo? No, use Eng) Articles 543 to 613 (Yuhan Hoesa / Limited Liability Company), Commercial Registration Act Articles 2, 45, 49 and Enforcement Rule, and the Electronic Commercial Registration Act where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Bureau, Seoul Central District Court
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation executed before a notary public, together with the Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company under the Commercial Registration Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean law imposes no minimum paid-in capital for a Yuhan Hoesa LLC. The subscribed capital must be fully paid at incorporation in cash or kind, but no blocked escrow account is required. For laboratory operation, the company must, however, maintain a funded current account sufficient to pay the ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation fee and civil defense installation costs.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHANG HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY)

Unanimously adopted at the statutory incorporation meeting held on the [day] of [month], 20XX, at the principal office, where the undersigned directors, being the statutory organizers, approve the following matters:

1. Subscription and Allotment of Equity Interests. The Board acknowledges that the entire initial capital has been lawfully subscribed by the initial members in the amounts set out in the membership register. Each subscription has been paid in cash to a licensed commercial bank. The Board confirms that no fractional or bearer interests are issued and all equity interests are fully paid. The funds shall be used exclusively to establish and operate an ISO/IEC 17025 accredited dangerous goods testing laboratory for UN38.3 battery safety and CE-RED electromagnetic compliance.

2. Banking Authorization. The Board authorizes the Representative Director and the Finance Director, jointly, to open and maintain corporate transaction accounts at a licensed Korean commercial bank. All wire transfer initiation and payment authorization shall require dual electronic signatures, and any non-operating disbursement exceeding 10,000,000 Korean won or 10,000 United States dollars shall first receive a board resolution, either prior or subsequent depending on the urgency.

3. Registered Office Adoption. The Board adopts the registered office located at [address], Seoul, Republic of Korea, as the statutory seat of the company for all legal service and regulator notice. The Representative Director is instructed to file the office adoption with the Seoul Central District Court commercial registration division and to notify the National Tax Service through the business registration process.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The Board appoints [name] as Representative Director with corporate custody of the seal and exclusive authority to represent the company, and [name] as Laboratory Technical Director with responsibility for laboratory quality, safety, and regulatory filing. Their term is three years, renewable by written consent.

5. Licensing Resolutions. Management is instructed to apply for the ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation, environmental registration, fire safety certificate, occupational safety clearance, and RF conformity registration required for the stated business scope. This resolution is immediately effective and may be revised only by a unanimous shareholder vote.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Clearance and Notarization of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registry Office of the Supreme Court of South Korea; licensed notary public in Seoul
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Internet Registry Office of the Supreme Court of Korea to search registered trade names and confirm that Yuhan Hoesa and the proposed trading name do not conflict with any existing entity. Draft the Articles of Incorporation in the statutory Korean format and include an object clause expressly authorizing UN38.3 battery drop testing, CE-RED electromagnetic laboratory operations, and ancillary technical inspections. State the par value and number of equity interests subscribed by each founding member. Execute the articles before a notary public, who will verify the identity of each subscriber, their passport, and the corporate seal if used. Notarization must be completed within two business days of execution, and the notarized articles must be retained in triplicate for court filing.
required_dossiers: Valid passport copy of each founding member
Individual seal certificate or authorized electronic certificate
Executed Articles of Incorporation in statutory Korean form
Trade name availability search report
Written power of attorney for a formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name search is rejected because the proposed name is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registration, file a revised name with an additional distinctive element through the same portal within one business day, then obtain a new notarized copy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Payment and Provisional Bank Account Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed domestic Korean commercial bank e.g. Shinhan Bank at the head office branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional cash account at a licensed Korean bank under the proposed company name. The Representative Director and Finance Director must appear in person, submit the notarized articles, and deposit the total capital by wire transfer. Obtain from the bank a capital deposit balance certificate showing the legal entity name, amount, and account administrator; the certificate is valid for three business days only. A formal director certificate is required for each cash contribution, supported by a banking transaction history or statement. This deposit mechanism is evidence of lawful capital subscription and is a prerequisite to the court registration filing.
required_dossiers: Provisional account application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Original identification documents of each subscriber
Wire transfer receipt or remittance advice for capital contribution
Director certification of lawful source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the case of an AML review, submit a source-of-funds memorandum, recent tax records, and bank statements to the branch compliance officer; the deposit certificate will be re-issued upon clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Bureau, Seoul Central District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for business registration with the Seoul Central District Court commercial registration division, either electronically through the court portal or in person. Submit the notarized articles, capital deposit certificate, lease consent letter from the building owner, and a statutory declaration from each director accepting office and confirming no disqualification. Pay the statutory registration fee and post it to the court account. The court will review under Article 45 of the Commercial Registration Act and issue a certificate of incorporation; obtain a certified company register abstract for use in tax and licensing filings. This step ensures the company acquires separate legal personality.
required_dossiers: Establishment registration application form (court standard)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of capital deposit balance issued within two business days
Consent letter from building owner for registered office
Lease contract or real estate copy of office
Statutory declaration accepting office by each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon issuance of a correction notice, cure each defect, such as notarizing a missing signature or submitting the lease consent, and resubmit online within five business days; registration will not recommence the general seven-day period after cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Business License Issuance and Permanent Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service District Office in Seoul; one licensed bank for permanent account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the corporate establishment notification with the Seoul National Tax Service district office within 28 days of commercial registration. Apply under the Hometax portal for a business registration certificate, selecting testing laboratory as the principal activity. Complete the VAT and corporate income tax recognition forms and request online electronic issuance authority for test reports. The National Tax Service will assign a business identification number and issue the business operator registration certificate. Use the certificate to open the permanent corporate bank account and to serve as a mandatory attachment in the KOLAS ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation application.
required_dossiers: Business registration application (Hometax)
Certified commercial registry abstract
Corporate establishment notification form
Registered lease agreement
Director appointment resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS rejects the business registration due to incomplete data, resubmit through Hometax after uploading corrected corporate abstract and lease; if the bank delays account activation, escalate to the branch manager with a board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Accreditation, Environmental Registration and Fire Safety and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Agency for Technology and Standards (KATS) via KOLAS; Seoul Metropolitan Government Environmental Bureau; National Fire Agency; National Radio Research Agency; Ministry of Employment and Labor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit to KOLAS/KATS a complete ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation package, including the quality manual, risk assessment, and calibration records for battery test chambers. File environmental registration with the Seoul Metropolitan Government environmental bureau, declaring any hazardous waste from lithium battery testing; if monthly waste exceeds 300 kilograms, the facility must register as a controlled waste generator. Obtain the National Fire Agency certificate after an on-site structural fire inspection, verifying fire-rated partitions, emergency evacuation routes, fire suppression for the battery test cell, and compatible hazardous waste storage. Verification of the RF measuring receiver is required from the National Radio Research Agency before CE-RED electromagnetic testing operations may begin. Each permit must be displayed at the registered office.
required_dossiers: ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation application and quality manual
UN38.3 and CE-RED test method validation reports
Environmental registration form or exemption declaration
Fire safety facility inspection application and building floor plan
RF equipment calibration certificate and receiver verification
Commercial registry abstract and business registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KOLAS identifies nonconformities, submit corrective action objective evidence within 30 days; if fire clearance is denied, install the recommended modifications and reinstate the inspection within 15 days; if radio emissions verification fails, recalibrate and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: KOLAS (Korea Laboratory Accreditation Scheme) under the Korean Agency for Technology and Standards (KATS), Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy; in coordination with the National Radio Research Agency of the Ministry of Science and ICT, and the local district government office in Seoul for business place licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ISO/IEC 17025 Testing Laboratory Accreditation Certificate under the framework of the Korean Accreditation System, combined with the Dangerous-Goods Testing Facility Business License obtained from the local district government on the basis of the NTS Business Registration Certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and the Seoul Metropolitan Government Environmental Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Environmental Registration for low-impact laboratory operation. A full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is not mandatory unless the facility handles more than 10 metric tons of hazardous chemical waste per year or operates fuel burners. In such cause, a Simplified EIA Report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) not to exceed 30 mg/L, Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) not to exceed 50 mg/L, suspended solids not to exceed 30 mg/L, and pH within 5.8-8.6. Air emissions: Volatile Organic Compound (VOC) concentration not to exceed 100 ppm at stack discharge and total odor concentration not to exceed 500 times dilution. Hazardous waste: spent lithium batteries must be fully discharged, packaged in UN-approved packaging, labeled as UN 3480 or UN 3481, and disposed of exclusively through MOE-licensed waste carriers using the electronic manifest system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Must obtain a Fire Safety and Fire Resistance Certificate from the National Fire Agency under the Fire Service Act, covering structural load inspection of the test floor, fire-rated wall integrity, emergency exit signage, automatic fire suppression for battery test cells, and ventilation for hazardous materials storage. Additionally, must obtain an Occupational Safety and Health clearance from the Ministry of Employment and Labor (MOEL) certifying compliance with Workplace Health Standard No. 29027, including laboratory chemical exposure limits, health surveillance for employees handling lithium batteries, and ergonomic design of drop-test stations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic filing and registration portal: HomeTax (Hometax) at www.hometax.go.kr; Korea Customs Service for export declarations through the UNI-PASS single-window system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity obtains its Korean tax identity either by incorporating a Yuhan Hoesa or by registering a domestic place of business of a foreign corporation. The NTS assigns one 10-digit Business Registration Number that functions as the corporate TIN, VAT registration number and employer registration number. The exhaustive procedure is: (1) complete incorporation of the Yuhan Hoesa or register the foreign corporation's domestic place of business with the competent registry; (2) appoint a Korean tax representative with a domestic address and execute a registered power of attorney if the foreign entity has no fixed domestic business establishment; (3) file the NTS-prescribed Business Registration Application with the competent District Tax Office, either through HomeTax or in person, within 20 days of commencing business or beginning VAT-taxable supplies; (4) attach the certified articles of incorporation, apostilled or consularized foreign registration certificate, proof of the Korean business address (lease or ownership), proof of foreign direct investment or share issuance, and the representative's identity documents; (5) for an export-only laboratory, identify the export zero-rating category on the VAT registrations and retain the planned evidence file; and (6) upon acceptance, receive the Business Registration Certificate with the final 10-digit number and confirm the active VAT registration in HomeTax. A foreign non-resident entity that has no Korean business establishment and supplies only electronic services to Korean consumers may instead use the simplified HomeTax registration procedure for non-resident electronic service suppliers, where that simplified category applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or similar pass-through election. A Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily classified as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is taxed at entity level on worldwide income. The only optional corporate election relevant to a wholly-owned domestic group is the consolidated corporate tax return regime for a domestic parent and its 100%-owned domestic subsidiaries. No hybrid mismatch election is available; hybrid mismatch adjustments operate mandatorily under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No revenue-based registration threshold (KRW 0) for a domestic corporation: a Yuhan Hoesa must register for VAT from the commencement of business regardless of turnover. For individual sole traders only, the simplified taxable person threshold is KRW 80,000,000 in annual taxable supplies, but such persons still obtain a business registration number.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The Value-Added Tax Act mandates the electronic tax invoice system. All VAT-registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices in the NTS-prescribed format and transmit them to the National Tax Service through HomeTax or through an NTS-certified ERP/API integration. The NTS validates the received data and uses the central electronic tax invoice matching database as the anti-fraud fiscal clearance mechanism; there is no separate physical fiscal stamp in Korea. Electronic tax invoices must be transmitted no later than the day following the supply date, except where the NTS quarterly or monthly aggregate filing rules apply, and B2C supplies are additionally reported through the mandatory NTS cash receipt system. Failure to transmit or non-compliant invoicing triggers statutory additional taxes and may lead to business suspension or criminal referral.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, zero-rating applies where: (a) goods are physically exported from Korea and the export declaration is accepted by Korea Customs Service; (b) services are supplied to a non-resident and the place of supply is deemed outside Korea, including qualifying technical testing and analysis services performed in Korea for an overseas principal when the results are delivered abroad and the consideration is paid in foreign currency through a Korean foreign exchange bank; (c) services are supplied for the export of goods, such as inspection and testing of export-destined batteries; and (d) qualifying offshore digital services are effectively used and enjoyed outside Korea. Zero-rated export status must be substantiated in the VAT return and preserves the input VAT deduction and refund entitlement. Supplies of otherwise zero-rated services to Korean consumers, or offshore digital services effectively used and enjoyed in Korea, remain subject to the standard 10% VAT and may require the non-resident entity to register under the simplified non-resident electronic service supplier procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service accepted Export Declaration (export clearance confirmation) generated in UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading for sea shipment or Air Waybill for air shipment showing the non-resident consignee and the Korean exporter
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list for the exported goods or re-exported test samples

Foreign exchange bank settlement confirmation or inward remittance receipt proving collection of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency (Korean equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate)

For exported testing services: signed service contract with the non-resident principal, delivery evidence of the test report or results, and foreign exchange bank remittance certificate showing payment for the service
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are jointly scrutinized by the National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service. The taxpayer must retain the complete export evidence file for the statutory record-keeping period and make it available on demand. If physical export is not proven, the service is found to be effectively used in Korea, or export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory 180-day period, the NTS will disallow the zero-rating, assess the unpaid VAT at the standard 10% rate, and impose statutory additional taxes. The misreporting surcharge can be as high as 40% of the underreported VAT for fraudulent non-declaration or false documentation, and up to 20% for negligent underreporting; the NTS may reopen a tax return for 5 years in ordinary cases and up to 10 years for fraudulent or omitted returns. In serious cases, the file is referred to criminal enforcement under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and corporate officers or the Korean tax representative may be subject to imprisonment and fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central monetary authority, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the statutory foreign exchange policy administrator under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; operational execution by designated foreign exchange banks and the Korea Customs Service through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised capital account with a rigorous reporting and surveillance framework rather than direct exchange controls. The Korean won is convertible for current account payments, trade settlements, service fees, dividends, and branch profit remittances, provided the transaction is routed through a designated foreign exchange bank and coded under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Capital account inflows, including equity contributions to a Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC, require either prior approval or a post-transaction filing with the designated bank, and the resulting foreign investment must be reported because the ultimate foreign owner is non-resident. For profit remittance, the blocking points are corporate tax clearance, audited financial statements, a board resolution approving the distribution, and documented underlying receivables; the bank will also query tax payments before any dividend outflow. Export proceeds in the service-export model represented by battery safety testing must be collected within 180 days of the service invoice date and repatriated to Korea unless the bank grants a foreign-currency retention approval. Although convertibility is high, inconsistent corporate purpose codes, late surrender of export proceeds, or unexplained cross-border flows will trigger financial intelligence unit reporting and account suspension, so treasury must maintain a complete evidentiary trail for every leg of the transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be received within 180 days from the date of shipment or, for services, from the date the service is completed and the invoice is issued. The proceeds must be surrendered to a designated foreign exchange bank and converted into KRW unless the exporter holds an approval to maintain a foreign currency account; standard mandatory conversion is effectively 100% in the absence of such approval. For UN38.3 battery testing and CE-RED electromagnetic laboratory services, each incoming payment must be matched against the testing service contract and filed under the current-account service purpose code, with test certificates and itemised invoices available for the bank's FEIS declaration and audit trail.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) and Trade Services Account
Capital Escrow Account for Inbound Equity Investment and Operational KRW Account
Foreign Currency Demand Deposit Account for Export Settlement
Corporate Current Account with E-Trade, FEIS Reporting, and L/C Services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury onboarding and prohibited for statutory Korean banking functions. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise or Revolut are not licensed as designated foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and cannot file FEIS declarations, issue Korean capital verification certificates, process KYC for a Korean resident corporation, or serve as the settlement account for Korean won disbursements. Wise may be used only as an auxiliary non-KRW payment rail for overseas vendor payments where the Korean entity maintains its principal corporate account at a licensed tier-1 bank and the bank-side reconciliation, beneficial owner verification, and tax declaration obligations remain at that licensed bank. This conditional use is not a substitute for the legally recognised banking infrastructure required for cross-border capital transactions in Korea.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch physical appearance by the statutory director or an authorised Korean-resident signatory is the general mandate for first-time Yuhan Hoesa LLC corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is available only in exceptional cases and requires notarised and apostilled powers of attorney, a video-call identity verification session, a Korean registered address, and a local corporate contact; in practice, most tier-1 banks will reject a fully offshore opening because the Financial Services Commission and KoFIU require the customer to maintain effective substance in Korea. The recommended path is a local Korean-resident director appearing at the designated branch with the board resolution, corporate seal, business registration certificate, and UBO declaration to secure the account within the first two weeks of incorporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner opacity and unsourced funding for the initial capital injection from foreign shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled UBO declaration, 12-month personal bank statements for each foreign shareholder, source-of-wealth explanation, corporate formation documents, shareholder register and beneficial ownership table, audited financial statements of any parent entity, tax identification numbers, and a board resolution authorising the capital payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived mismatch between the declared laboratory business and the technology/gaming-oriented customer base producing inbound digital-content style payments instead of clear testing fees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed battery safety testing agreements, UN38.3 test plans and summary reports, CE-RED electromagnetic procedure records, calibration certificates for testing equipment, invoices and payment schedules, customer onboarding evidence including KYC certificates, and a detailed revenue recognition schedule proving that all income corresponds to actual physical laboratory work.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure from receiving lithium battery samples or sending test reports to customers in OFAC, EU, and Korean prohibited-address jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening declarations proving no sanctioned jurisdictions in the customer and supplier base, dangerous goods transport documentation, customs import and export records, safety data sheets, end-user certificates for regulated battery cells, and contractual clauses prohibiting re-export to restricted entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin substance of a newly incorporated foreign-owned LLC with no local payroll, no laboratory equipment, and no physical lease or insurance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for the laboratory premises with rent payment receipts, utility bills in the company name, payroll records for at least two technical staff, equipment ownership titles or leasing contracts, professional testing facility insurance, ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation or pending-application evidence, and an audited or certified opening balance sheet showing tangible asset acquisition.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder should execute a SWIFT MT103 transfer to the Korean entity's Capital Escrow Account at a designated foreign exchange bank, using the direct-investment or equity-contribution purpose code required by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The bank will check the remitter and beneficiary names, UBO declaration, board resolution, and source of funds, then issue a certificate of foreign exchange purchase after the funds are credited. The next step is capital verification by a certified Korean public accountant or bank treasury officer, followed by FIPA registration with the Help Center for Investment or the designated bank if the equity contribution exceeds the statutory foreign investment threshold; lower-value contributions must still be declared through the Foreign Exchange Information System. Only after capital verification should the funds be swept into the operational KRW account, and every inbound payment must be traceable back to the approved capital injection to avoid future dividend-repatriation complications.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outgoing trade and service payments should use SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers with the correct Korean foreign exchange purpose code and supporting invoices, contracts, and, where applicable, customs declarations. For large purchases of battery testing hardware or CE-RED measurement equipment, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued through the tier-1 Korean bank is the preferred clearing rail because it protects advance payments and holds the supplier to documentary compliance. Documentary collections (D/P and D/A) are acceptable for established suppliers with a reliable trade history where full L/C cost is unjustified. For all outbound payments, the bank will require the underlying service agreement, supplier due diligence, and proof that the payment is consistent with the entity's declared testing laboratory operations; the business manager must retain copies of every certificate and test report related to the settled invoice.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable KRW/USD forward contracts of up to 12 months for hedging genuine current-account exposures arising from export invoices and equipment import settlements, permitted through the designated bank upon submission of underlying trade contracts.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW/USD are available only where the counterparty is offshore and the Korean entity proves a genuine underlying business exposure, with the transaction documented and reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act derivative business rules.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps and plain-vanilla currency swaps are permissible solely for hedging real cross-border loan principal and interest positions, not for speculative profit, and require board approval, bank suitability assessment, and derivative transaction reporting to the authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Meeting of Members - approval of financial statements and appointment of management members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Commercial Act; minutes and financial statements retained at the registered office; Commercial Court Registration Office only for event-driven registrations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year entity, on or before 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic administrative strike-off for failure to hold the meeting, but management members become civilly liable for unlawful distributions; repeated refusal to comply with a court order may result in enforcement fines, judicial dismissal of management members, and in extreme cases judicial dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; calendar-year filers must file and pay by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surcharge of 20% of the unpaid tax; unfaithful underreporting surcharge of 10%; fraudulent underreporting surcharge of 40%; late-payment surcharge of 3% plus 0.022% per day on the unpaid amount; sustained non-filing and non-payment may lead to NTS seizure of bank accounts and receivables, nullification of the Business Registration Certificate, and administrative strike-off through compulsory collection or judicial liquidation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the Si/Gun/Gu where the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the corporate income tax return; calendar-year filers must pay by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 3% of the unpaid local tax plus additional daily arrears charges; prolonged delinquency can trigger bank account freezes, seizure and auction of corporate assets, refusal of local tax certificates, and suspension or nullification of business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25 April of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid or unfaithfully reported VAT attracts an additional 10% on the unpaid amount plus 0.03% per day; two consecutive semi-annual non-filings with no reported business activity may be treated as dormancy and trigger Business Registration Certificate nullification or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT first-half final return for January-June, including April-June transactions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25 July of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing and underreporting penalties identical to the preliminary return regime; unpaid VAT attracts 3% non-payment surcharge plus daily arrears; continued failure may lead to NTS collection seizure and administrative deregistration of the business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25 October of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT surcharge of 10% on unpaid or understated amounts plus daily interest; repeated non-filing permits NTS to issue an assessment, seize assets, and nullify the business registration certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT second-half final return for July-December, including October-December transactions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25 January of the immediately following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Final VAT non-payment triggers the 3% non-payment surcharge plus 0.03% per day; false final returns attract 40% fraudulent-reporting penalty; sustained non-compliance can result in NTS-led administrative strike-off of the corporate registration and forfeiture of the business license.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company) is subject to compulsory statutory independent audit under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, etc. if total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million at prevailing exchange rates). There is no separate statutory turnover or headcount trigger for a limited liability company under the External Audit Act; however, if the company is converted into a stock company and listed on KOSPI or KOSDAQ, an external audit is mandatory irrespective of size. In addition, a certified audit may be contractually required by domestic Korean lenders, a K-IFRS consolidated parent company, holders of debt instruments, or a UN38.3 testing accreditation body if audited financial evidence is required for laboratory approval or insurance coverage.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) or Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP). K-IFRS is mandatory for listed companies and for certain large audit-subject companies; a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa may apply K-GAAP. Revenue from battery safety UN38.3 testing and electromagnetic laboratory services must be recognized in accordance with Korean Accounting Standards No. 1115, which aligns with IFRS 15. Any statutory audit must be performed by a Korean certified public accountant in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA) issued by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Korean Commercial Registration system does not require an annual beneficial-ownership return. Beneficial ownership information is collected by Korean financial institutions under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information for anti-money-laundering purposes. The company must maintain a register of members at its registered office, and any transfer of membership interests must be recorded in that register before the transfer is enforceable against the company and third parties. A transfer of Korean membership interests to a non-resident or any change of a foreign shareholder's name, shareholding amount, or nationality must be reported to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA/Invest KOREA within 30 days under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Any change in the registered office, management members, or corporate objects must be filed with the local Commercial Court Registration Office within two weeks of the triggering event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges, Pledges and Mortgages over Membership Interests

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,200 per year for Korean corporate secretarial service and registered-office mailbox service; full physical office premises in Seoul would be additional.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per year for a Korean certified public accountant audit under K-GAAP or K-IFRS if the KRW 12 billion asset threshold is exceeded; if the threshold is not exceeded, only voluntary review or agreed-upon-procedures costs may apply.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22% national corporate income tax for taxable income exceeding KRW 200 million; 10% bracket below KRW 200 million; 20% bracket between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; plus 10% local surtax on national tax
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 50% corporate tax reduction for 5 years in free economic zones or foreign investment zones; R&D expense deduction of 25% to 50% for qualified battery safety testing and electromagnetic research; patent box regime taxing qualified patent income at a reduced effective rate of 3% to 5%; foreign direct investment cash grants under Foreign Investment Promotion Act; tax credit for capital investment in high-tech testing equipment

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Tax Return Form 101 (법인세과세표준및세액계산서) and Local Income Tax Return supplementary form; electronically lodged through HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr) on the National Tax Service Internet portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending December 31, the return is due on or before March 31 of the following year; an extension of up to 6 months is available upon application, but any tax due must be paid before the original deadline and estimated tax prepayments are required for corporations with prior-year tax liability above thresholds

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification information, registered address, business registration number, fiscal period covered, business activity code (ISIC 7120 for technical testing and analysis), legal form (Yuhan Hoesa / LLC), and number of foreign shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If foreign shareholders own 10% or more of the issued shares, a Schedule of Foreign Investors must be attached, showing name, tax residence, and ownership percentage. Failure to disclose foreign ownership may trigger penalty under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and deny later DTA claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement summary: gross sales, cost of sales, gross profit, selling and general administrative expenses, non-operating income, non-operating expenses, ordinary income, and net income before tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a battery safety testing laboratory, accrued fees from overseas clients must be recognized on a gross basis. Any transaction with a non-resident related party must be separately itemized and must reflect arm's length pricing; a protective TP adjustment may be entered as a reconciliation item here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: adjustments to taxable income (加算 and 減算) including non-deductible expenses, exempt income, bad debt allowances, depreciation adjustments, and special reserve reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the lab paid royalties, management fees, or intercompany service charges to a non-resident parent, the applicant must prove economic substance and justify that the fee is not a disguised dividend. Unsupported payments will be disallowed, added back to taxable income, and treated as constructive dividend subject to 22% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward calculation, carryback offset, and taxable income determination before tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners cannot use Korean tax loss carryforward to offset income later repatriated as dividends; the loss realisation remains inside the Korean entity. If the entity has been a pure shell with no operations, the National Tax Service may deny loss claims and impose a 40% negligence penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, DTA relief, and special tax credits (e.g., R&D credit, employment credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean company itself may claim foreign tax credit for taxes paid by its foreign branch, but non-resident shareholders generally cannot credit Korean withholding taxes on dividends against their home country tax unless the DTA provides for foreign tax credit. Must attach Form D-1 (claim for taxes paid in a foreign country) with official foreign tax receipt or TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate tax due at the applicable progressive rates, plus 10% local surtax, after deducting prepayments and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a wholly non-resident owned Yuhan Hoesa, this amount must be paid before forwarding funds abroad. Any cash distribution declared in the general shareholders meeting must be reported in Form 13 (withholding on foreign corporation dividends); the payer must withhold 22% if no treaty reduction is approved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing documentation and related-party transaction schedule: controlled transactions, amount, method used (CUP, Resale, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split), and margin range.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory to attach Schedule of International Intercompany Transactions (B-Form) when aggregate controlled transactions exceed KRW 5 billion. Non-resident related parties must provide a Service Agreement, License Deed, or cost allocation methodology and demonstrate contractual substance. Failure to attach exposes the entity to TP penalty of up to 30% of the adjustment amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director signature, agent information, and final declaration that the information is true and complete.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean resident director or the designated tax representative in Korea must sign. A non-resident CEO cannot sign electronically without a Korean tax identification number. Knowing false statement can trigger criminal liability under Article 103 of the Framework Act on National Taxes (up to 3 years imprisonment).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 20% of the unpaid tax for fraudulent non-filing, 10% for underreporting, and 0.03% simple daily delinquency surcharge for each day of delay up to a maximum of 45% of the unpaid amount. Non-payment of tax due by apost-final date triggers seizure; criminal fraud for wilful omission: fine up to 3 times the evaded amount and imprisonment up to 3 years. Continued failure to provide transfer pricing documentation draws a KRW 10 million fine plus a 10% adjustment surcharge.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax + 2% local surtax) on cash and constructive dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; reduced to 0% in certain tax-free reorganisations only after pre-approval by the Ministry of Economy and Finance
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Taxation Agreement, the recipient must (i) obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the home jurisdiction issued in the same calendar year; (ii) complete Form BD-8 'Application for Exemption/Reduction of Withholding Tax' or the electronic equivalent on HomeTax; (iii) file a Beneficial Ownership Certificate demonstrating that the recipient has legal and economic rights over the income and is not a conduit through a zero-tax jurisdiction; (iv) provide attestation that the intercompany loan, licence or service arrangement has arm's length terms; (v) obtain the NTS confirmation of treaty eligibility before or simultaneously with the dividend distribution order; (vi) retain the dividend distribution resolution and payment evidence for 5 years. For dividends paid to a corporate shareholder owning at least 25% of the Korean entity for 12 months prior to distribution, the treaty rate is normally 5%; for portfolio shareholders the rate is 15% (or 10% if the DTA so specifies). The reduction is applied only after the NTS has accepted the filing; otherwise the full 22% is withheld and a refund claim must be filed within 35 days of the remittance date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 22% (20% national tax + 2% local surtax) and royalty or technical service fee 22% (20% + 2%). Under most Korean bilateral treaties (e.g., US-Korea, UK-Korea, Germany-Korea) the limit is 10% for interest and royalties; in some treaties royalty on industrial, commercial or scientific equipment is limited to 5%, and technical fees used by an industrial operation may be treated as business profits and exempt if no permanent establishment exists. To apply the lower rate the payee must obtain a KR TRC and submit documentation proving full beneficial ownership; otherwise the higher statutory rate is withheld and a refund process may take 3 to 6 months.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File preparation when the aggregate amount of controlled transactions (including sales of goods, purchases of services, intangible licence fees, and loans) exceeds KRW 5 billion in a fiscal year; Master File required when the aggregate amount exceeds KRW 50 billion; Country-by-Country Reporting required for multinational groups with consolidated global revenue above KRW 1 trillion (or USD 850 million equivalent).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although South Korea does not apply a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulation, the substance-over-form principle is embedded in the Framework Act on National Taxes and the International Tax Adjustment Act. A battery safety testing lab performing UN38.3 drop tests must demonstrate Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in Korea: possession of licensed test chambers, qualified electrical safety engineers, operational decision-making offices in Korea, physical performance of drop, shock, vibration and crush testing, and maintenance of project data and test reports on Korean soil. If the Korean entity merely forwards invoices to a foreign related office while testing is performed elsewhere, the NTS may recharacterise the revenue as foreign PE income, impose TP adjustment, deny the treaty benefit, and treat the entity as a shell liable for penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Test Certificate Fabrication and Revenue Omission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing UN38.3 battery safety certificates without actually conducting the drop, shock, vibration, thermal or altitude tests; invoicing a portion of fees via unregistered personal accounts in a third country; under-reporting service revenue from foreign battery manufacturers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 103 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and Article 66 of the Corporate Tax Act, the National Tax Service may impose a negligence penalty of 40% of the underreported tax and an unlawfully claimed refund penalty of 40%; criminal fine up to 5 times the evaded amount and seizure of the testing equipment and bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ordered or participated in falsification are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of all evaded tax and penalties; the NTS can impose a travel ban (destination restriction) and blacklist the director as habitual defaulter; criminal conviction carries imprisonment for a term of up to 3 years (or 5 years for aggravated fraud under the special tax offence law).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Default and Thin Capitalisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing, without just cause, to prepare and submit the Local File, Master File or CbCR for intercompany fees beyond the statutory thresholds; artificially inflating interest payments to a non-resident parent by capitalising the lab with excessive shareholder loans instead of equity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Adjustment Act Article 11: infringement surcharge of up to 30% of the transaction value and an income adjustment year causing an additional tax of 10% of the adjustment amount; Article 18 thin capitalisation rule disallows interest on loans exceeding twice the equity investment from a non-resident controlling shareholder, adding the excess to taxable income and applying a 22% withholding tax on deemed dividend.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for gross negligence in maintaining transfer pricing documentation, and the court may pierce the corporate veil if the entity is operated as an alter ego of the foreign parent. Principal directors face civil asset restitution up to the total unpaid amount and a criminal sentence of imprisonment up to 1 year for failure to comply within 60 days of a demand order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Shell Company Concealment – Beneficial Ownership Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Cayman or Hong Kong shell to route testing fees from Korean battery manufacturers so that the Korean lab is structured as a registered agent only, while actual control and profits reside in a hidden offshore beneficiary; deliberately omitting the foreign beneficial owner in the financial institution's Know-Your-Customer files when opening a Wise or wire payment account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign Exchange Transactions Act Articles 9 and 17 impose a fine of up to KRW 100 million, and the Financial Intelligence Unit may suspend payment rails; proceeds hidden in overseas accounts are subject to forfeiture; a criminal penalty for money laundering under the Proceeds of Crime Act Article 25 carries a non-conditional fine of up to KRW 200 million and imprisonment for a term of not less than 3 years up to a maximum of 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directorship in a shell where the actual economic owner is concealed converts limited liability into unlimited personal liability; courts order the director to restore all repatriated sums, place the director on the FIU blacklist banning bank transfers and international travel, and if the concealment is convicted as wilful money laundering the director faces imprisonment for a minimum of 3 years, asset confiscation, and disqualification from serving as a corporate director for 10 years.
